english.notes:
(i) For further guidance see the prosecution guide.
(ii) In the first instance a prohibition notice under section 22 of the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 should be applied in accordance with HSE policy. Failure to comply with that prohibition should result in prosecution. Care should however be taken to obtain evidence to prove that the operator in the interim period had not complied with and therefore discharged the prohibition notice.
(iii) Where there is evidence of multiple offences, blatant disregard of the regulations or there has been previous advice, prosecution should also be considered.
(iv) It is appropriate to establish if the driver has been issued with a valid training certificate. If this has been done and the operator has been informed of the failure to carry the valid training certificate then this can be dealt with by verbal warning. If the issue of a valid training certificate cannot be verified then a penalty notice is appropriate until it can be produced.
(v) ADR 2009 section 8.2

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
